title: Korean Interference 3: Cluster Production — No Vowel Insertion

slides.teacher_cue: What sound? Lips together, then pop open — voiced.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /b/ cleanly.
slides.correction_move: Model /b/ with lips together and pop. Students repeat three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for devoicing — /b/ must be voiced. b is the onset in bl clusters.

slides.teacher_cue: What sound? Tongue tip touches ridge — air flows around both sides.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /l/ with tongue tip contact at the alveolar ridge.
slides.correction_move: Model /l/ with mirror — tongue tip contact visible. Students repeat three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /r/ substitution. /l/ is the second consonant in most l-clusters today.

slides.teacher_cue: What sound? Tongue curls back — no contact with roof.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /r/ with tongue curled back, no contact.
slides.correction_move: Model /r/ with mirror. Students repeat three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution. /r/ is the second consonant in gr, pr, tr, fr, br clusters.

slides.teacher_cue: What sound? Upper teeth on lower lip — air escapes. Voiceless.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /f/ cleanly.
slides.correction_move: Model /f/ with upper teeth on lower lip. Students repeat three times.
slides.observation_note: Note: f/p Korean interference may also be active. Watch for /p/ substitution for /f/.

slides.teacher_cue: Play night once. Replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write night accurately — note igh trigraph.
slides.correction_move: Replay night once, segment orally n-igh-t, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for correct spelling of igh and for voiced final t.

slides.teacher_cue: Play sharp once. Replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write sharp accurately.
slides.correction_move: Replay sharp once, segment orally sh-ar-p, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for sh digraph at onset and for the ar vowel team.

slides.teacher_cue: Play chair once. Replay only if needed before checking.
slides.expected_response: Students write chair accurately.
slides.correction_move: Replay chair once, segment orally ch-air, then recheck.
slides.observation_note: Watch for ch digraph and for the air vowel team.

content_payload.front_text: bl  cl  fl  gl  pl  sl

slides.teacher_cue: This is the key rule for English clusters: two consonants come together with NO vowel sound between them. Korean phonology tends to insert a short vowel — 'buh-lack' not 'black'. You must hold both consonants together in one movement. bl = [bl] as one unit, not [b][uh][l].
slides.expected_response: Students understand the no-vowel-insertion rule and attempt each cluster as a single unit.
slides.correction_move: Model each cluster label — say it once cleanly, then say the epenthesis error, then the correct form again. Students repeat the correct form chorally.
slides.observation_note: Watch for any vowel insertion between cluster consonants. This is the primary target for this lesson.

content_payload.correction_routine: black is correct — bl blend with no vowel between. buh-lack inserts a vowel — that is the Korean epenthesis error to avoid.

slides.teacher_cue: Play both. Which is correct English? Students choose A.
slides.expected_response: Students identify A (black) as the correct English production.
slides.correction_move: Play each again. Model black slowly — bl as a single unit. Students repeat three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students can auditorily discriminate the epenthesis error from the correct cluster production.

content_payload.correction_routine: grip is correct. guh-rip inserts a vowel between g and r.

slides.teacher_cue: Play both. Which is correct? Students choose A.
slides.expected_response: Students identify A (grip) as the correct English production.
slides.correction_move: Play each again. Model grip slowly — gr as a single unit. Students repeat three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for epenthesis discrimination — gr cluster here vs bl cluster in 03-02. Both cluster types must be heard correctly.

slides.teacher_cue: Say black. The bl cluster is one unit — no vowel between b and l. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say black with clean bl onset and connect meaning.
slides.correction_move: Model bl slowly as a single movement. Students repeat black three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for vowel insertion between the cluster consonants — 'buh-lack' is the epenthesis error.

slides.teacher_cue: Say clap. The cl cluster is one unit — no vowel between c and l. Mime clapping. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say clap with clean cl onset and connect meaning.
slides.correction_move: Model cl slowly as a single movement. Students repeat clap three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for vowel insertion between the cluster consonants — 'cuh-lap' is the epenthesis error.

slides.teacher_cue: Say flag. The fl cluster is one unit — no vowel between f and l. Show or describe a flag. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say flag with clean fl onset and connect meaning.
slides.correction_move: Model fl slowly as a single movement. Students repeat flag three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for vowel insertion between the cluster consonants — 'fuh-lag' is the epenthesis error.

slides.teacher_cue: Say glow. The gl cluster is one unit — no vowel between g and l. Mime a warm soft light. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say glow with clean gl onset and connect meaning.
slides.correction_move: Model gl slowly as a single movement. Students repeat glow three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for vowel insertion between the cluster consonants — 'guh-low' is the epenthesis error.

slides.teacher_cue: Say plan. The pl cluster is one unit — no vowel between p and l. Use in a sentence: I have a plan. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say plan with clean pl onset and connect meaning.
slides.correction_move: Model pl slowly as a single movement. Students repeat plan three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for vowel insertion between the cluster consonants — 'puh-lan' is the epenthesis error.

slides.teacher_cue: Say slim — thin. The sl cluster is one unit — no vowel between s and l. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say slim with clean sl onset and connect meaning.
slides.correction_move: Model sl slowly as a single movement. Students repeat slim three times.
slides.observation_note: Watch for vowel insertion between the cluster consonants — 'suh-lim' is the epenthesis error.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build clap left to right. The cl is one unit.
slides.expected_response: Students build clap correctly: cl | a | p.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting of clap, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students treat cl as a single unit — no vowel insertion when building.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build flag left to right. The fl is one unit.
slides.expected_response: Students build flag correctly: fl | a | g.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting of flag, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students treat fl as a single unit — no vowel insertion when building.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build plan left to right. The pl is one unit.
slides.expected_response: Students build plan correctly: pl | a | n.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting of plan, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students treat pl as a single unit — no vowel insertion when building.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sounds and build slim left to right. The sl is one unit.
slides.expected_response: Students build slim correctly: sl | i | m.
slides.correction_move: Return to oral segmenting of slim, then rebuild one sound at a time.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students treat sl as a single unit — no vowel insertion when building.

slides.teacher_cue: I is a sight word. All other words decodable. Two cluster words: clap and plan.
slides.expected_response: Students read "I can clap and plan." accurately — cl and pl clusters with no vowel insertion.
slides.correction_move: Model the sentence once, then return to one-to-one word tracking.
slides.observation_note: Watch for vowel insertion on clap (cuh-lap) or plan (puh-lan).

content_payload.text_content: The flag is slim. He held the plan.

slides.teacher_cue: The, the, He are sight words. All other words decodable. Cluster words: flag, slim, plan.
slides.expected_response: Students read both sentences accurately — fl, sl, pl clusters with no vowel insertion.
slides.correction_move: Model each sentence once, then return to one-to-one word tracking.
slides.observation_note: Watch for vowel insertion on flag (fuh-lag), slim (suh-lim), or plan (puh-lan).

content_payload.text_content: She can clap. The slim flag fell.

slides.teacher_cue: She, The are sight words. All other words decodable. Cluster words: clap, slim, flag.
slides.expected_response: Students read both sentences accurately — cl, sl, fl clusters with no vowel insertion.
slides.correction_move: Model each sentence once, then return to one-to-one word tracking.
slides.observation_note: Watch for vowel insertion on any cluster word. Three cluster words in close succession is a strong test.

content_payload.title: Close the Lesson

check_items.label: What is vowel epenthesis and why must we avoid it in English clusters?
Say each word: clap, flag, plan, slim. No vowel insertion.
Say one sentence using a cluster word from today.

content_payload.notes_field: Check: can students explain epenthesis? Are all four cluster words produced cleanly? Is the oral sentence accurate?

slides.teacher_cue: Close with concept recall, production check on all four cluster words, and one oral transfer sentence.
slides.expected_response: Students explain epenthesis in their own words, produce the four cluster words cleanly, and construct one sentence with a cluster word.
slides.correction_move: If any cluster triggers vowel insertion, isolate that cluster, drill it as a unit, then re-attempt the word before closing.
slides.observation_note: Watch for whether students can verbalize the rule, not just produce it. Note students who need continued cluster drilling in future lessons.
